newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ALLIN CLAIMS HIS FIRST CAREER SENIOR PGA TOUR TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ALLIN CLAIMS HIS FIRST CAREER SENIOR PGA TOUR TITLE.

text.p: Bud Allin captured his first career Senior PGA Tour event with a one-shot victory Sunday at the $1.2 million Senior Invitational tournament.

The 52-year-old Allin, who began the day with a three-shot lead, fired a three-under-par 69 in the final round to finish at 11-under 205. One shot back after shooting a tournament best 67 was Jim Colbert, the Seniors' 1996 Player of the Year.

Allin gained entry into the field only when Gibby Gilbert withdrew just before the start of the event. Allin cashed in on his unexpected opportunity and grabbed a first-prize check of $180,000 for his first professional win of any kind since the PGA Tour's 1976 Pleasant Valley Classic.
Bruce Summerhays, Mike Hill and Jim Albus tied for third at eight-under.
Heading into the par-four 18th hole, Allin had a one-shot lead over Colbert. His five-iron approach landed 60 feet from the pin. His first putt stopped two feet short.
"The putt at 18 looked like two miles," said Allin. "My nerves were shaky at 18 but I was close enough on the final putt to know I'd make it."
